newsitem.title: USA: Court to rule on Smith Corona plan today.
newsitem.headline: Court to rule on Smith Corona plan today.

text.p: Smith Corona Corp could emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection as early as Feb 7 if its reorganization plan were approved by U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Helen Balick at a hearing today.
The hearing is scheduled to begin at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.

On the effective date of the plan, the company's new stock would begin trading and the old stock would be cancelled. Company spokeswoman Rivian Bell told Reuters an application has been made for the new stock to trade on NASDAQ.
"We have no idea what the stock will trade at. We'll have to wait and see," Bell told Reuters.
There are objections to the plan, but an attorney for the official committee of unsecured creditors, Neil Glassman, told Reuters the committee hopes the court will overrule the objections.
"We see no problems that the debtor can't surmount," Glassman said.
The Class Eight or general unsecured creditors hold allowed claims of about $33 million.

According to Bell, these creditors would be paid $0.30 on the dollar in pro-rated cash distributions from a pool of $10.78 million. In addition, the class would receive 85 percent of the new common stock to be issued on the effective date of the plan.

Included in the Class Eight category of $33 million in allowed claims are $9.85 million for trade and general creditors, $8.35 million for the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corp and $14.85 to settle disputed claims, Bell said.
Current shareholders would receive one warrant for every 20 shares of Smith Corona stock they now hold.
The warrants would be priced at $8.50 and shareholders could exercise them during an 18-month period that would begin six months after the company emerged from bankruptcy.
If and when the new stock reached $8.50 a share, Class Eight creditors would have received full value for their allowed claims, Bell said.

"The creditors committee is solidly behind the plan. The major objections have been settled...There are a large number of unsecured claimants who believe they are entitled to more than the company believes they are entitled to...We hope the court concurs with our assessment," Bell said.

Smith Corona, of New Canaan, Conn., makes personal word processors, portable electric typewriters, label printers and other office, home and school accessories. The company filed for Chapter 11 protection on July 5, 1995, listing assets of $207.9 million and liabilities of $198.9 million, according to court papers.
